before: A pseudo-class selects an element in a particular state. It begins with a colon.

:hover matches when a pointing device is over an element. A keyboard user may never hover over it.
```css
a:hover { text-decoration: underline; }
```
:focus matches the element receiving keyboard input. :focus-visible matches when the browser decides a visible focus indicator is needed.
Do not remove the browser’s focus indicator unless you provide another visible one. A hover style alone is not a keyboard focus indicator.

:disabled matches a disabled control.
```css
button:disabled { opacity: 0.6; }
```
The HTML disabled attribute controls availability; dimming alone does not disable a button.
For the practice, keyboard-tab to the input and look for the outline. Inspect the disabled button separately. Automated focus checks do not prove every keyboard interaction works.
after: A pseudo-class chooses an element in a certain state. It starts with a colon. A state describes what is happening to the element, such as being pointed at or receiving input.

Focus marks the part currently ready to receive input. `:focus` matches the focused part. `:focus-visible` matches when the browser decides a visible focus mark is needed, such as during keyboard use.
Keep the browser’s focus mark unless you replace it with another clear one. A hover style alone is not enough. A keyboard user needs to see which control Tab has reached.
Press Tab to reach the note input and look for its navy outline. Check the disabled Save button separately. Passing a basic check does not replace trying the page with the keyboard.

before.question: A form shows a helpful border only on input:hover. A person uses Tab to reach the field without moving a mouse. What is missing?
choices: A focus indicator for keyboard interaction
A second hover rule with a darker color
A disabled attribute on the input
before.explanation: Hover depends on pointing interaction. Keyboard focus is a different state, so a visible focus style is needed without disabling the field.

after.question: A field shows a border only on hover. Someone reaches it with Tab and does not use a mouse. What is missing?
choices: A disabled attribute on the field.
after.explanation: Keyboard focus and hover are different states. The focused field needs a visible mark.

changes.before: Use Tab in the preview to verify the focus indicator without a mouse. Browser heuristics control :focus-visible. The automated check focuses a text input; it does not simulate all keyboard and pointer paths.
changes.after: Use Tab in the preview to check the focus outline. The browser decides when `:focus-visible` matches, so also try pointer use.
